text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Macedonian President Kiro Gligorov invited by U.S. President Bill Clinton to visit Washington.

- Macedonian MPs refused to discuss the opposition Liberal Democratic Party's proposed resolution on early elections. The party proposed assembly dismissal on September 15 and early elections in mid-November.
- Anti-government demonstrations planned in centre of Skopje on Thursday by the largest opposition party IMRO-DPMNY.
- "If the government and President Gligorov do not respond to our demands for early elections, anti-government demonstrations will be held every day," IMRO-DPMNY spokesman Dragi Ivanovski said.
- The ruling SDAM (Social Democratic Alliance of Macedonia) said the demonstrations "endanger the institutions of the system and the peaceful and democratic development of Macedonia.

- Melting of snow in the mountains on the Macedonian-Albanian border brought invasion of Albanian refugees. Macedonian police on Wednesday detained a group of 75 Albanian refugees and 11 Yugoslav Albanians from Kosovo province who illegally crossed the border. -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
